title: perf(canary): auto-detect latency/throughput regressions and add rollout guards
author: Aisha Khan
description:
Context: We run continuous performance canaries across our serving fleet to detect regressions in latency and throughput before rolling out new releases. Over the last quarter we observed a couple of incidents where small tail-latency regressions slipped through canaries because the detection thresholds were static and rollout logic lacked an automatic pause/fallback when regressions were detected.

This PR introduces two related improvements: 1) an adaptive regression detector that automatically tunes sensitivity based on recent noise and workload variance; and 2) rollout guards that pause/rollback canary rollouts when the detector flags a statistically significant regression in latency or throughput. The goal is to reduce false negatives (missed regressions) while keeping false positives (unnecessary rollbacks) low by using workload-aware thresholds and cooldown windows.

What changed (high level):
- New detector: performance/canary/detector.py and detector service glue in performance/canary/service.py. Detector computes rolling-quantile deltas and applies a noise-aware significance test.
- Rollout guards: canary/orchestrator now supports a "pause_on_regression" policy; the coordinator will automatically stop a rollout, mark the canary as degraded, and trigger a fast rollback to the previous model variant.
- Telemetry: added canary.perf.regression_detected metric, canary.rollout.pause_reason tag, and dashboards/alerts updates.
- E2E tests: added perf_canary_detector_test and an integration test that simulates noisy traffic and a regression injection.
- Docs: updated docs/perf-canaries.md with guidance for tuning sensitivity and examples.

Motivation and tradeoffs:
- We intentionally keep the detector lightweight and server-side so it can run co-located with canary workers. We avoid complex Bayesian models to reduce operational surface area; future work could replace the detector with a more sophisticated learner if needed.
- Rollout pause is conservative: we add a cooldown period (configurable, default 10m) to prevent oscillation on transient spikes.

Acceptance criteria / checklist:
- [x] Detector computes quantiles and flags regressions as expected in unit tests.
- [x] Rollout pauses and triggers rollback on flagged regressions in integration test.
- [x] New metrics emitted and dashboards updated.
- [x] Feature gated behind runtime flag (perf.canary.auto_detect_enabled) and off by default for a 2-week staged rollout.

Related: ENG-4321 (improve canary coverage), ENG-4398 (rollout safety improvements), incident SUP-1284 (March canary slipup).

Hook detector into canary service and add rollout pause logic
Integration test for noisy traffic regression detection
review_comments: Marco Li: Overall looks good - can you justify the choice of a rolling-quantile test vs a mean-based t-test?
Aisha Khan: Rolling quantiles are more robust to skewed latencies and intermittent spikes; added a comment and a brief benchmark in tests/ to compare false-positive rate.
Sofia Martinez: Can we make the cooldown configurable per-customer? Some Dedicated deployments want shorter windows.
Aisha Khan: Exposed cooldown as canary.rollout.cooldown_seconds in runtime flags and documented recommended ranges.
Rajat Singh: CI flaked once on the integration test (timing). Recommend increasing slack in the test harness.
Aisha Khan: Increased test timeouts and added a retry in the harness; CI green after rerun.
release_notes: Added adaptive canary regression detector and rollout guards to pause/rollback on significant latency/throughput regressions. Feature gated off by default; configurable cooldown and sensitivity settings.
notes: Feature gated (perf.canary.auto_detect_enabled=false) to allow staged rollout to 10% of traffic
On-call runbook updated (docs/oncall/perf-canaries.md) with steps to inspect canary.perf.regression_detected metric and force-unpause if needed
risk_assessment: Low-medium: conservative defaults and cooldown reduce risk, but incorrect sensitivity tuning could cause unnecessary rollbacks. Recommend close monitoring during staged rollout.
backcompat_notes: No API breaking changes. New metrics and runtime flags are additive.
changelog_entry: perf(canary): adaptive regression detector + rollout guards (ENG-4321, ENG-4398)
estimated_impact: Should reduce missed regressions during canary rollouts and lower incident rate for small tail-latency regressions. Initial rollout set to 10% of canaries for 2 weeks.
additional_context: This change was driven by SUP-1284 where a tail-latency regression in a minor model variant caused increased 99th percentile latencies for some customers until manual rollback. The new detector recreates that scenario in integration tests and verifies automatic rollback.
